newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Husband of Ershad lover seeks Bangladesh divorce.
newsitem.headline: Husband of Ershad lover seeks Bangladesh divorce.

text.p: The husband of the lover of former Bangladeshi president Hossain Mohammad Ershad wants a divorce, a marriage registrar official in Dhaka said on Thursday.

Mosharraf Hossain, a former industry secretary and lawmaker, signed the notice to be divorced from Zinat Hossain on Wednesday at the registrar's office and put it immediately in the mail, registrar Syed Shariatullah told reporters.
The separation would come into effect in three months unless the couple settled their differences and reaffirmed a desire to live together, he said.
He declined to give further details. Neither Zinat nor her husband were available for comment.

Zinat, in her late 40s, is a legislator in Ershad's Jatiya Party, which is an ally of the ruling Awami League of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina. Her husband is a legislator from the main opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party headed by former prime minister Begum Khaleda Zia.
Zinat's affair with Ershad, 68, had been an open secret for years. Ershad recently told a Dhaka newspaper that he had proposed to marry Zinat to formalise a 14-year relationship.
He caused unease in and outside his party when he recently celebrated his birthday with Zinat instead of his wife of more than 40 years, Begum Roushan.

Three top party leaders, including two former prime ministers, have demanded he quit his party chairmanship, citing the extramarital affair and his dictatorial management. Ershad has proposed a dialogue with the rebels trying to patch up the conflict. The rebels say they will impose a set of conditions for sitting down to talks.
Lieutenant-general Ershad, who seized power in a 1982 bloodless coup, was ousted in a 1990 popular uprising and sent to jail. He was freed last January.
Ershad and wife Roushan are both members of parliament.
